messages.subject: Makefile updated
parts:
I spent the last 2 days really working through the makefile. I think
it's in a better state now. At the very least, I understand make much
better.

The changes should not really affect how you currently build.

The biggest changes are:
- separate variable declarations for the 3 operating systems
- dependencies are autogenerated

If you want OS specific flags, there are 3 files (mac, win, linux)
under src/makefile that set specific flags based on the OS. The OS is
automatically detected, but to force it from the command line, set the
variable OS to either mac, win, or linux.

The result of the dependencies being autogenerated should help us with
compile time for unit tests. We shouldn't need to clean before running
the unit tests again. Any changes to source files will trickle down
and force recompilation of any test that requires it. Also, the target
is now "test-unit". I have left "test-all" in there as the same
target, but my intention is to have "test-all" run a more
comprehensive test in the future.

The test-bugs target runs all the bugs examples. This is what Jenkins
runs in the mornings. It is not currently able to finish all bugs
models. I am working through them slowly so we can detect when changes
to the code base stop our models from running.

Daniel

I can't install g++ 4.6 on that machine, but I can install 4.4.x and

That said, requiring 4.6 because of one build failure seems premature.
It's not as if the test builds but yields a wrong answer. If defining

recent).

Ben
